<!-- pr-reviewer: 3fa2631c0f65cff2d18dacc8dd168ada2379e493 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** I reviewed only the three commits on top of #784 (c261f6fe, 28b5e682, 3fa2631c), trial-merged with `upstream/main` (merged cleanly).

### What looks good
- `march::shell_in` uses the same half-open bracket as `parity_of` (`c > z`): `(cm, ca]` for a top and `(ca, cm]` for a floor. So a mesh-only sign flip always has a crossing to read, and `Unreadable` is reachable only through a cut with no record. That matches the decision record.
- The broken-promise exits in both `refine` and `refine_down` return the last proven-air height. That over-reports material, which is the safe direction. `cut_downs` (a moved `cut_ups` bisection, which keeps the proven-inside side) puts the floor at or below the true cut top, so it errs safe as well.
- The bounded-tool refusal is still there: `cut_near(floor)` in `column_span`, and in `sliver` any claimed centre refuses when `bounded_cuts` is set. After this PR, the only thing that sets `bounded_cuts` is the tool's own flag (`field_turn.rs:143`).
- The pins catch real mutations. I changed `cn - d` to `cn - 0.5 * d` and 1 `field_floor` test plus 1 `carry_engine_agreement` test failed. I dropped the `d == 0.0` skip and 2 + 2 failed. I removed the level-facet branch in `plane_claim` and `a_level_facet_crosses_at_exactly_its_height` failed.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. All files are under 400 lines (`march_up.rs` is 130) and new modules carry a provenance line. No snapshot, golden or process-file changes. The body has `Changelog:` and ends with `Fixes #780`.

### Local results (merged with main, macOS, debug unless noted)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| sim lib | 69 passed (includes `solid_rest` 8 and the `field_turn` unit test) |
| sim `carry_engine_agreement` | 10 passed |
| sim `field_floor` | 10 passed |
| sim `field_carry` / `field_body` | 9 / 6 passed |
| sim `stock_backend_parity` | 13 passed |
| sim `stock_carry` / `stock_sim` / `stock_sdf` | 7 / 24 / 9 passed |
| sim `hidden_rest_banded` / `ridge_rest` / `scan_arc` | 5 (1 ignored) / 4 / 2 passed |
| sim, the other 16 suites in the quick plan | 152 passed, 0 failed |
| motion `posed_subtract` | 1 passed |
| app `stock_export` / `verify` / `setup_carry` / `carried_verify` / `rest_across_setups` | 2 / 21 (2 ignored) / 9 / 8 / 7 passed |
| app `stock_engine_agreement`, release `--ignored` | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **`march_up` under-reports a flipped floor where the cell probe is exactly 0, and lifting E2a's refusal exposes it** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/march_up.rs:111-112`, with `field_turn.rs:143`).
   - **The shortcut.** `if phi == 0.0 { return ReadUp::Floor(z) }` copies `march`'s "the probe landed ON the surface" shortcut. But the probe's magnitude belongs to the cell, so `phi == 0` means the cell *centre* lies on a mesh plane, not that `z` does. The ascent returns whatever height it reached inside that cell.
   - **Scenario.** A plate `cube((0,0,-6.25),(20,12,0))` at cell 0.5, so the old floor -6.25 sits on a centre. Cut a flat r 2.0 slot along y 6 at z -5.8, then bake the flip `y -> -y, z -> -z`. At `column_span(10.25, -6.25)` the true material is [5.8, 6.25].
   - **What it reads.** This PR answers `Material { top: 6.4406, floor: 6.05 }`, so 0.25 of steel reads as air. The `floor: 6.05` comes from the `phi == 0` exit; I traced it locally. #784's head (80a79a15) answered `CutFromBelow` here.
   - **How widespread.** Across a sweep of plate floors {-6, -6.25, -6.1, -6.3, -5.9}, tops {0, 0.25, 0.1, -0.2} and slot depths from 0.5 below to 3 above the floor, 13 flipped configurations under-report the floor by 0.05 to 0.25. All have the floor on a centre (-6.25), and #784 refused every one of them by name.
   - **Fix.** Treat `phi == 0` as "this cell's centre is on a surface", not as a floor at `z`. Refine from the cell (`refine_down` from its centre), or answer `Unreadable`. Do the same for the `p == 0.0 => Floor(z_hi)` arm at `:120`.
   - **Pin.** Add a `field_floor` fixture with a stock plane on a cell centre: the slot above, flipped, with the floor within 1e-6 of 5.8. The cut-after-flip fixtures all use block planes on cell boundaries, so they never reach this exit.
   - **Until then,** keep E2a's `bounded_cuts` on a flipped bake. The answer to "can the interim refusal be lifted?" is not yet.

### Commit 3 (`solid_rest::plane_claim`) impact
- **Callers.** `column_crossings`, which feeds the field engine's `shell_crossings` (`field.rs:223`), and with it `march`, `march_up`, `column_span` and the march verdicts. Also `scan_hidden`, the hidden-rest scan behind `scan::hidden_rest`, through `plane_claim` and `crossings_from_claims` directly. `camcraft-app` only re-exports the module (`lib.rs:73`). The column engine's heightfield does not call it.
- **What moves.** Only a facet whose three z are equal, and only by the ulp the barycentric sum rounded. Pairing, `Open`/`Paired` and the 1e-9 level clusters are unchanged in practice.
- **Verdict at a point exactly on a level face.** `parity_of` counts `c > z`, so the law is half-open [floor, top).
  - On a level top face, a point exactly at the plane could read inside when the sum rounded up; now it always reads outside, which is the law.
  - On a level floor face, a point exactly at the plane could read outside when the sum rounded up; now it always reads inside, which means more material, the safe direction.
  - Either way the change is a zero-measure set brought into line with the stated law, not a flip on any open region.
- **Results.** `stock_engine_agreement` in release `--ignored` passed 3/3 on the merged tree. `hidden_rest_banded`, `ridge_rest`, `stock_sim` and `stock_sdf` are green.
- **Caveat (not blocking).** `crossings_from_claims` averages a level's claims (`sum / count`). With 3 or more claims of one off-lattice level at a shared vertex (5.1 + 5.1 + 5.1, then / 3), the mean can still miss `z` by an ulp. The pin's 21x21 grid includes the diagonal (2 claims, exact) but no vertex where 3 or more facets meet.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **A pre-existing defect on `main` (not caused by this PR).** `march`'s own `phi == 0.0 => Read::Top(z)` (`march.rs:241-242`) has the same flaw upright. On `cube((0,0,-6.25),(20,12,0))` with a flat slot at -6.0, `column_span(10.25, 6.25)` reads `Material { top: -6.25, floor: -6.25 }` where [-6.25, -6.0] stands. The same happens at #784's head, and `march` with that line is on `main` (it feeds `march_verdicts` and `columns`). The field engine is not the default, but this deserves its own issue, and the fix above should probably go in both marches.
- **Upright verdicts are not byte-identical for off-lattice floors.** That is expected from the shell-crossing read, but the body says the upright path is byte-identical. On a -6.3 floor, two configurations went from `Unreadable` to an exact read and one (slot at -6.25) went from a read to `Unreadable`. None under-reports.
- **Off-lattice plates still over-report their top by up to ~0.2.** For example, a 1.8..2.2 plate reads top 2.24 and a 2.0..2.25 plate reads 2.44. These come through the broken-promise path, because the probe's parity is taken at `z`, not at the cell centre. This is the safe direction and identical at #784's head; it is only a note against "exact to rounding".
- The PR title says `refactor`, while #780 is filed as a `feat` with enhancement labels. `Changelog: none` fits, since no shipped verdict changes; the type is for the merger to choose.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: dc4873e74ece40e9aacab493b0d39f08686f7fa7 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** This is a delta review of 3fa2631c..dc4873e7 (`march::walk`, the centre-only walk), trial-merged with `upstream/main` (it merged cleanly). I reviewed it as new code because the fix is structural.

### What looks good
- **The air-skip proof is sound.** I checked it against `field_gen` (`field_gen.rs:19-41`, Dial buckets with relaxation at `:131-139`):
  - A stored magnitude at a centre is at most the truth plus sqrt(3) cells (exact seed within SEED_R, then hops of cell/sqrt(3) <= the straight length).
  - Cells past the horizon answer `cap`, and their truth exceeds `cap`. So for an outside centre, truth >= mag - 1.732c.
  - `clear = floor(mag/c) - 2` gives a skipped extent of at most `(clear - 1)c`, below truth by more than 1.27c. The landing centre is also inside the proven ball.
  - The proof covers every point of the skipped run, not just its centres, so a skip cannot jump over a web of any thickness.
- **The claim-skip is sound.** A claim is the negated tool distance (`field_cut.rs` max law). Inside, every pose distance is exact or under-reads (`field_solid.rs:17-25`: the taper's `-min(|g1|, h - zl)` at `:192-193` is a lower bound on depth; flat and bull are exact). The golden-section minimum only shrinks the claim, so a ball of radius `claim` around the centre is removed. Note the claim proves a ball, which covers more than "the centre and its half-line", and the code skips only `floor(claim/c)` cells.
- **The bracket.** The centre before the first material centre is always proven air, either probed or inside a proven run. The `face` read is unchanged.
- **Termination.** The walk is bounded by `BRACKET_WALK` = 8192 centre visits (was 4096 sub-cell steps). Each visit advances at least one cell, and the cost per visit is one parity count plus two hash lookups. There is no hang path. `cells_of` clamps before the `as i32`, and the index math saturates.
- **The pins are real.** With the five source files reverted to 3fa2631c, both new pins fail: `a_stock_plane_on_a_cell_centre_reads_exactly_on_both_sides` (field_floor.rs:246) and `no_column_under_reports_across_plates_and_slots_on_and_off_the_lattice` (:290).
- **#824's own scenario is fixed on the verdict path.** In my `Stock::top` sweep, every plate with its floor on a centre (-6.25) reads exactly or over. No numeric under-reads remain anywhere in the sweep, down from 377 on `main` and 244 on 3fa2631c.
- **Other changes.** The `sliver` ceiling change (`center < ceiling`, field_floor.rs:177) is consistent with the half-open law.
- **Laws.** Files are under 400 lines (march.rs 291, march_up.rs 70). There is no new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in src. Provenance lines are present, and the decision file `docs/decisions/780-field-march-up.md` is updated. No process, snapshot, golden or dependency changes.

### Local results (merged with main, macOS, private target)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| sim lib | 69 passed |
| sim `field_floor` | 12 passed |
| sim `carry_engine_agreement` | 10 passed (8-turn bit-identity holds) |
| sim `field_carry` / `field_body` | 9 / 6 passed |
| sim `stock_backend_parity` | 13 passed |
| sim `stock_sdf` / `stock_sdf_cut` / `stock_sim` | 9 / 12 / 24 passed |
| sim `hidden_rest_banded` | 5 passed, 1 ignored |
| app `verify` / `setup_carry` / `carried_verify` | 21 (2 ignored) / 9 / 8 passed |
| app `stock_engine_agreement`, release `--ignored` | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **A floor skin with no cell centre inside it now reads as no material on the verdict path. On `main` and 3fa2631c it read as material.** (`march.rs:236-245`; consumers `march_verdicts.rs:64,123`, `columns.rs:163`, `march.rs:279`)
   - **Where it comes from.** `walk` probes only centres. When the skin left under a cut holds no centre, the walk steps from the claimed centre above it to the air centre below it. It answers `NoMaterial`, which every consumer reads as NaN: "nothing stands here".
   - **What already handles it.** `column_span` catches this through `field_floor`'s sliver law, and the 432-read pin goes through `column_span`. `Stock::top`, `deviate_field`, `measure_field`, the sheet and `Stock::columns` (the rest and program masks, the feed-engagement sampler) all go through `march` alone.
   - **Scenario.**
     - The stock is an 8 x 6 plate from z -6.05 to 0 at cell 0.5 (`FIELD_BAND`), and a flat r 2 slot along y 3 is cut at z -5.8, which leaves [-6.05, -5.8] standing.
     - The part is `cube((0,0,-7),(8,6,-6.0))`, so 0.2 of it is rest.
     - `Stock::deviate(part, 0.01)`:
       ```
       dc4873e7 (this PR): dev under the slot NaN, rest_cells 64,  128 of 192 columns NaN
       3fa2631c:           dev under the slot 1.5, rest_cells 128, 0 NaN columns
       ```
     - So the whole slot footprint reads "no verdict", and the rest under it is not reported. That is an under-report in a verdict, and the rest mask would treat that steel as air.
   - **How widespread.** I swept `Stock::top` over floors {-6, -6.25, -6.1, -6.3, -5.9, -6.05, -6.2}, tops {0, 0.25, -0.2, 0.1, -0.05} and 19 slot depths from 0.5 under the floor to 3 above it, reading three columns under the slot and one beside it (2660 reads).
     - 128 reads that were material on both `main` and 3fa2631c (an over-read such as -4.5, or the exact top) now read NaN.
     - Examples (floor / slot): -6.05 / -5.8, -6.1 / -5.85, -6.1 / -6.0, -6.2 / -5.9 through -6.19.
     - Skins between 0.01 and 0.3 thick are affected.
     - The other 412 NaN reads were already NaN on `main`. For example, a plate with its floor at -6.0 cut to -5.8 is NaN on all three heads, so that part of the gap is older than this PR.
   - **Fix (suggestion).** Before `walk` (or `column_top`/`march` for a descent) answers `NoMaterial`, read a centre-less sliver the way `field_floor::sliver` already does: from the shell crossings in each air-to-air step and the `up_at`/`down_at` records. For example, `march` could fall back to `column_span`'s top when the walk finds no material centre but the column's shell crossings are non-empty. If the sliver cannot be placed, it should over-report (the record's height, or the shell crossing) rather than return NaN.
   - **Pin.** Add a `Stock::top`/`deviate` pin (not `column_span`) on the scenario above, so the column under the slot reads >= -5.8 and the rest is counted. Extend the same assertion over the existing 432-config sweep through `Stock::top`.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **#824.** Its "Done means" (no under-read when a stock plane sits on a cell centre) holds in my sweep, both through `Stock::top` and through `column_span`, flipped too. It can close with this PR once item 1 is fixed, since item 1 is on the same verdict path. Until then I would keep `Refs #824`.
- **The walk budget.** The field does not cap its Z extent (`lattice_of` caps XY only). A column that crawls one cell per visit, outside the shell with magnitude under 3 cells (a narrow deep bore), and is taller than 8192 cells answers `Unreadable`/NaN. That is the same class as the old 4096-step budget, so I note it rather than block on it.
- Test-only: the shared `target/` hazard is real. When I ran a second tree on one `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, cargo reused the other tree's `camcraft-sim` without a rebuild, so give any comparison run its own target.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 03437938a1e013ec19a82ab515523ab0fca7a5d7 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a delta review of dc4873e7..03437938 (`march::centreless` and the shared sliver law), trial-merged with `upstream/main`. The merge was clean. The round-2 blocker is fixed on every verdict path I could reach.

### What looks good
- **`centreless` covers both `NoMaterial` exits of `walk`** (`march.rs:267-274`): the last centre before the world's end, and a proven run that reaches the end. The function itself is at `march.rs:285-302`. Its outcomes:
  - The shell never crosses the column: `NoMaterial`. This is the same `shell_extent` the old `column_span` used.
  - Mesh-only (`cuts == false`): the shell's extreme crossing, an over-read or exact for any plane.
  - Otherwise `sliver`: `Material` gives `Top`; `Empty` gives `NoMaterial`; `CutFromBelow` or `Unreadable` gives `Unreadable`. A column the shell proves material can no longer leave the walk as `NoMaterial`.
- **`sliver`'s `Empty` really means "proven cut through", for spanning tools.** A pair contributes nothing only in two cases:
  - A centre reads `u == 0` or `d == 0`, so it lies inside a cut that spans that whole half-line (the monotone law).
  - `pair_lo > pair_hi`. The entries come from `field_ray`'s bisection, which reports a proven-inside point. So `c + u` is at or above the true cut bottom and `cn - d` at or below the true lower-cut top. Both ends err toward more material, so an inverted pair is truly empty.
  - Bounded tools never reach that logic: any claim in `k0..=k1` refuses first (`field_floor.rs:201`).
- **`column_span`'s `NoMaterial => Empty` arm is equivalent to the old `=> sliver` arm** (`field_floor.rs:129`):
  - The walk now returns `NoMaterial` only from `sliver`'s `Empty`, called with the same `shell_extent`. The "shell never crosses" exit cannot fire there, because `column_span` returns `Empty` before marching (`:116`).
  - Where `sliver` finds `Material`, the walk now returns its top and `column_span` re-derives the floor. With no `cut_downs`, every `Material` sliver has the shell floor as its floor (an interior pair without `entry_down` refuses), so the result is identical. With `cut_downs`, `march_up` reaches the same `sliver` call through `centreless`.
  - No sliver that `column_span` used to read is dropped. The only visible change is below under notes.
- **The pins are real.** With `crates/sim/tests/field_skin.rs` copied onto dc4873e7, both fail: `a_floor_skin_under_a_slot_is_a_verdict_on_every_path` at :57, the `Stock::top` NaN under the slot, and `no_column_the_shell_proves_reads_nan_or_air_through_stock_top` at :116. Both pass on this head.
- **Laws.**
  - march.rs is 328 lines, field_floor.rs 254, field_skin.rs 206: all under 400.
  - No new `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in src. `shell_extent`'s `unwrap_or` is a fallback.
  - The new suite carries a provenance line and a gate map.
  - `docs/decisions/780-field-march-up.md` records review fix 2 with what was considered and dropped.
  - No process files, snapshots, goldens, dependencies, build.rs, scripts or `.github` changes.

### Sweep through the verdict path (`Stock::top` and `Stock::deviate`; release; each head in its own worktree with its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`)
- **Fixture.** An 8 x 6 plate at cell 0.5 with floors {-6, -6.25, -6.1, -6.3, -5.9, -6.05, -6.2} and tops {0, 0.25, -0.2, 0.1, -0.05}. A slot along y 3 (r 2) at 19 depths from 0.5 under the floor to 3 above it, so skins of 0.01 to 0.3 are included.
- **Reads.** Seven columns: four under the slot (y 3.25, 4.25, 1.75, 1.25), one off-lattice (4.4, 2.6) and two beside it.
- **Tools.** Flat and ball, upright and flipped (the flip through the baked `turned`): 9310 reads each way. On top of that, `deviate` against the plate's own bottom on every upright fixture, counting NaN columns where the shell proves material.
- **Headline.** "Under" counts on-lattice reads below the truth. "NaN on material" counts NaN where material stands.

| Head | Upright: under / NaN on material | Flipped: under / NaN on material | `deviate` NaN columns on material (runs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (e2d655e5) | 921 / 754 | (no flip API) | 18852 (299) |
| 3fa2631c | 389 / 754 | 0 / 630 | 18784 (290) |
| dc4873e7 | 0 / 1190 | 0 / 1530 | 31040 (380) |
| **03437938 (this PR)** | **0 / 0** | **0 / 0** | **0 (0)** |

- **NaN on this head.** It occurs only where the column is truly cut through (805 reads each way). Material never reads where the truth is air, and the largest over-read is 4.5e-13.
- **Bull nose, r 2 with corner 0.5, same grid.** This head reads 3990 of 3990 exactly with 0 NaN on material and 0 `deviate` NaN; dc4873e7 had 595 NaN reads and 175 `deviate` runs with NaN.
- **Taper.** No NaN on either head. The taper is bounded and leaves the plate top standing above it, which is what the field reads.
- **The off-lattice ball column (4.4, 2.6) is not a regression.** It reads 560 heights under the exact ball surface. Every one of them is the ball's depth at that cell's centre column (dy 0.25, `z + 0.01569`): the cut records are per cell, and `Stock::top` off a centre reads its cell's record. `main` shows the same thing (395 reads, the rest NaN). The verdict readers only sample at centres.

### Local results (merged with main, macOS, private target)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| sim lib | 69 passed |
| sim `field_floor` / `field_skin` | 12 / 2 passed |
| sim `carry_engine_agreement` | 10 passed |
| sim `field_carry` / `field_body` | 9 / 6 passed |
| sim `stock_backend_parity` | 13 passed |
| sim `stock_sdf` / `stock_sdf_cut` / `stock_sim` | 9 / 12 / 24 passed |
| sim `hidden_rest_banded` | 5 passed, 1 ignored |
| app `verify` / `carried_verify` | 21 (2 ignored) / 8 passed |
| app `stock_engine_agreement`, release `--ignored` | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **#824 can close with this PR.** Its "Done means" holds: no under-read when a stock plane sits on a cell centre (floor -6.25, top 0.25, slot floors landing on centres such as -5.75), upright and flipped, through `Stock::top`, `deviate` and `column_span`. It is pinned by `field_floor::a_stock_plane_on_a_cell_centre_reads_exactly_on_both_sides` and by the `field_skin` sweep. The commits say `Refs #824` and the body says only `Fixes #780`. To close it on merge, add `Fixes #824` to the PR body (a body edit, not a push), or close it by hand after the merge, naming 03437938.
- **`Unreadable` and air look the same to the consumers.** `deviate_field` skips the column (`march_verdicts.rs:61-63`), and `column_top` and `Columns::top_at` give NaN. So a sliver that the records cannot place (a bounded tool's skin, a missing record) still leaves the rest counts and masks silently, just as `NoMaterial` did.
  - This is the existing "Unreadable is NaN" law and nothing in my sweep reaches it with spanning tools.
  - The decision file's line "`Unreadable` blocks the same way NaN did but is a named refusal" is true of the enum, not of what a verdict reports. It may be worth a follow-up issue so `Deviation` counts or refuses unreadable columns before the field engine becomes the default.
- **A small refusal-name change in `column_span`.** A centre-less column where a bounded claim falls in `k0..=k1` but not within a cell of the floor used to return `CutFromBelow` (and `FloorRead::CutFromBelow`). It now returns `Unreadable`. Both are refusals, and the decision file records it.
- **Not covered by this delta (unchanged).** A multi-crossing (undercut) column with a sub-cell flange above a deeper material centre reads the deeper centre's top. The PR body already lists it under "Not exercised".

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
